- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from high to low, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid lagged correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
